about.title: Personal Injury Help in San Juan Capistrano, California
about.longDescription: San Juan Capistrano's mix of historic streets and busy regional corridors means collisions happen more often than residents might expect. Public records show 141 injury collisions in the most recent final year, leaving 171 people hurt and 2 people dead. Traffic tends to bunch up along I-5, Camino Capistrano, Ortega Highway, and Del Obispo Street, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. seeing more reported crashes than other times. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, or in a slip-and-fall, dog bite, or other accident somewhere in the city, sorting out next steps while you're still recovering is hard. That's where we come in. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people in San Juan Capistrano with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened. There's no cost to talk with someone, and any attorney you're connected with typically works on contingency, meaning no fee unless they recover money for you. You focus on healing; let someone else help sort out the rest.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Deadline
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim in California. Claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened — your share of fault simply reduces your recovery, it doesn't eliminate it.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not limit the amount you can seek for non-economic harm like pain and suffering, unlike some other states.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to you, and they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in San Juan Capistrano?
items.answer: In most California personal injury cases, you have two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If a government agency was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible doesn't automatically bar you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Are there certain areas in San Juan Capistrano where crashes are reported more often?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along I-5, Camino Capistrano, Ortega Highway, and Del Obispo Street, with more reports typically logged on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in standard personal injury cases, so compensation can reflect the actual impact of your injuries.

items.question: Does it cost anything to use LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney — we are not a law firm and don't charge for the connection. Attorneys in the network generally work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money.
